headline: Flyers place Cam York on injured reserve
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Flyers have placed defenseman Cam York on injured reserve, noting he was averaging 21:49 of ice time through five games in 2026-27.

That workload matters because PHI is in rough shape without any further subtraction: 1-6-3 for 5 points through 10 games, with a 38.3 percent share of expected goals and a 34 percent share at 5-on-5. York has not been the problem so far this season, exactly, but he hasn't been the solution either. With the team on the ice, PHI controlled just 26.29 percent of 5-on-5 expected goals when he played, and the team's share of expected goals was 10.59 percentage points better with him off the ice. He has no points and 0.41 expected goals of his own over five games. That is a tiny sample, but it points to a defender soaking up minutes without driving play. For the Flyers, the real question is who absorbs nearly 22 minutes a night and whether that changes anything. For fantasy, York's value was already thin, with 26 points last season, so this costs little.
